Mobile game ad formats: the 5 that work in 2026
Tomas Hubka
Last updated: Sep 03, 2026
min read
The 5 mobile game ad formats that actually work in 2026. Short-form video, rewarded, playable, playable end cards, and interstitial. What to run, when, and how to research each.
The mobile game advertising ecosystem in 2026 is dominated by a small set of high-performing formats. Short-form video carries most of the spend. Playables punch far above their share. Rewarded video is the default acquisition channel for a large share of developers. And a group of formats you might still see on older ad-format lists (banners, native, offerwalls, splash) have moved out of the user acquisition conversation into monetization, where they now belong.
This guide covers the 5 mobile game ad formats that actually drive user acquisition in 2026: what each one is, when to use it, and how to research what your competitors are running with it. For the network-served formats covered below (video, rewarded, playable, playable end cards, interstitial), tools like
Ad Insights
let you study exactly what competitors are running in your genre right now.
The state of mobile game advertising in 2026
Before choosing which formats to run, it helps to know the three forces currently shaping performance across every one of them.
Short-form video dominates spend. Video creatives account for 74% of all mobile game ads, and short-form clips under 30 seconds make up 58% of that. If you're deciding where to invest first, this is the format most of your competitors are already testing hardest.
Creative lifespan has collapsed. In mature markets like the US, UK, and Germany, the average creative burns out in under 5 days. Teams shipping fewer than 4-6 creatives per month are losing performance to teams that ship 20-40. Format choice matters less than refresh cadence at this point.
Two production styles now shape every format. UGC-style creative (creators filming themselves reacting to gameplay in the visual language of TikTok and Reels) accumulates fatigue 30-40% slower than studio-produced ads of the same volume. Alongside it, AI-generated variations are expected to make up more than 50% of shipped creatives by the end of 2026. Neither is a format, but both apply across every format below.
The 5 dominant formats in 2026
1. Short-form video ads
The single most common format across the mobile game advertising ecosystem. Short-form videos run 6 to 30 seconds, are optimized for the first three seconds (the hook), and dominate spend on Meta, TikTok, Google, AppLovin, and Unity Ads. Meta's algorithm judges ad similarity largely based on the hook, so the opening frames do double duty: they hook the viewer and they tell the platform what audience to serve the ad to.
Best fit:
every genre, every campaign type, especially for driving installs from new audiences. Casual and hyper-casual titles lean heaviest on this format; midcore and RPG games use it alongside longer-form gameplay video.
How to research it:
In
Ad Insights
, filter the creative gallery for video creatives in your genre and region, then sort by impression estimate to see which short-form creatives are driving the most reach in the market right now. Study the opening three seconds across the top performers, and pay attention to how they use text overlays, captions, and pacing.
Video ads gallery in Ad Insights
2. Rewarded video ads
A rewarded video gives the player an in-game reward (currency, energy, extra life) in exchange for watching. Because players opt in, rewarded video consistently delivers the highest eCPM of any format, typically $10-30 CPM in top-tier markets. 82% of developers report that reward-based UA vastly outperforms traditional channels.
Best fit:
in-app monetization inside hybrid-casual, casual, and mid-core titles with mid-session moments that pair naturally with a value exchange (energy refills, revive after failure, currency rewards). Also increasingly used for user acquisition through reward-based UA networks.
